title: Ain't Done Dancing Yet
stanzas: Black suit hanging by the bedroom door
Shined my shoes like I did before
Told that mirror, “Man, we got one more”
Walked in slow when the band kicked in
Some young boy gave me half a grin
I just smiled and let the night begin
Ain’t done dancing yet
Still got fire in my step
Turn that rhythm up, I’m not through yet
No, I ain’t done dancing yet
Started with a shoulder, then I moved my feet
Took one small step when I felt that beat
Then that backbeat hit me good and deep
Lady in red said, “You still got time”
I said, “Baby, I still got mine”
Then we caught that groove and held it tight
Ain’t done dancing yet
Still got trouble in my step
Let that backbeat roll, I’m not through yet
No, I ain’t done dancing yet
Young folks standing by the bar
Watching me move from where they are
One good turn and they knew who we are
I don’t need to jump, I don’t need to spin
Just find that groove and settle in
Been doing this since way back when
Ain’t done dancing yet
Still got Saturday in my step
Let that horn line blow, I’m not through yet
No, I ain’t done dancing yet
Jacket open, tie hanging loose
Whole room moving to that old blues
Those old black shoes still knew the moves
Clock said late, but I stayed right there
Sweat on my brow, smoke in the air
Band hit the break, I was still right there
Ain’t done dancing yet
Still got living in my step
Turn that whole room up, I’m not through yet
No, I ain’t done dancing yet
Ain’t done dancing yet
Still got midnight in my step
Let those horns blow hard, I’m not through yet
No, I ain’t done dancing yet
Not through yet
No, not through yet
I ain’t done dancing yet
No, no no, not through yet
Still got the blues in me
I ain’t done dancing yet

title: Memphis Knows My Name
stanzas: I was seventeen down on South Main Street
Black shoes shining, Memphis under my feet
Five dollars in my pocket and no place I had to be
Music came spilling through an open door
Piano and guitar rolling out across the floor
I didn’t know the players, I just knew I wanted more
Memphis knows my name when I come back around
Old streets start talking when I roll into town
Sixty years behind me, I’m still that boy in this town
Eddie had a Ford that shook at every light
Smoke behind us, three boys packed in tight
We burned half the evening just deciding where to ride
Ruby wore perfume from the corner store
Sat beside me laughing with her feet up on the door
I forgot what she told me, but I remember wanting more
Memphis knows my name when I come back around
Every old corner brings a memory down
Sixty years behind me, but that feeling hangs around
We sat by the river when the night got hot
Passed one cold bottle, talked about what we had not
Thought we knew the whole world from that little riverside spot
Now there’s silver where my black hair used to be
I move slower now, but Memphis still gets me
One good backbeat and the years fall off of me
Memphis knows my name when I come back around
I hear my younger footsteps somewhere in that sound
Sixty years behind me, but they never left this town
Some names stayed with me, some slipped away
Some I still can picture like I saw them yesterday
Funny what comes walking back when an old song starts to play
Memphis knows my name when I come back around
Every beat reminds me where my roots went down
Sixty years behind me, but Memphis knows me now
Memphis knows my name when I come back around
That old river keeps on rolling through this town
Sixty years behind me, and I still know that sound
Memphis knows my name
Memphis knows my name
Yeah, Memphis still knows my name

title: One Of Those Crazy Nights
stanzas: Friday night, we found a little place
Piano man had panic on his face
Said, “Lost my band! Can you take their place?”
Eddie grabbed the bass, Joe took the drums
I shook that tambourine till my fingers went numb
Three old fools, but we got it done
It was one of those crazy nights
Nothing made sense, but it felt all right
Three grown fools with no end in sight
Yeah, one of those crazy nights
Everybody dressed in Sunday best
I said, “Man, these folks sure look impressed”
Then a lady in white came in with the rest
Somebody yelled, “Here comes the bride!”
Eddie looked at me with his eyes open wide
We'd crashed a wedding and played right through!
It was one of those crazy nights
Wrong kind of gig, but the music was right
Nobody stopped us, we played all night
Yeah, one of those crazy nights
The groom shook my hand, said, “You boys are great!”
His mama brought us each a dinner plate
We ate like kings and stayed up late
The bride took my hand for the final dance
The groom just laughed, said, “Give him a chance!”
I said, “Son, I don't turn down a dance!”
It was one of those crazy nights
Three old fools in the wedding lights
Bride was dancing by my side
Yeah, one of those crazy nights
It was one of those crazy nights
Oh, one of those crazy nights
Don't ask me why
Don't ask me how
I'm still laughing about it now

title: That's How Rumors Start
stanzas: Eddie caught me buying a ring
“Who's the lucky lady?” I didn't say a thing
He left like he'd heard everything
He told the barber I'd met someone new
The barber said, “A wedding's coming soon”
By lunch, the neighbors said it must be true
That's how rumors start
One little grin, they play their part
They add a little, then pass it through
Now folks know my plans before I do
Joe said, “Best man? I can do that!”
Miss Ruby asked where she'd buy her hat
I said, “What wedding?” — they just stared back
My wife said, “So who's the bride?”
I said, “You, baby.” She rolled her eyes
“That's what they all say!” she replied
That's how rumors start
One little grin, they play their part
The whole town's planning my wedding day
And nobody asked what I had to say
She read our wedding date inside
Both our initials, side by side
She kissed me, said, “I'd be your bride”
I told Eddie, “My wife said yes again”
He told the barber and all his friends
Left out “my wife” — here we go again!
That's how rumors start
One little grin, they play their part
I cleared it up, but it didn't last
Now the second rumor's spreading fast
That's how rumors start
Oh, that's how rumors start
One little word
And the whole town talks
“Eddie! The SAME wife!”

title: It's Better Than Ever
stanzas: She said, “Friday, I've got plans for two”
I said, “Honey, I've been planning too”
She winked and said, “That's why I married you”
Some folks grab a bite and call it fun
Before they've tasted much, they're done
We like five courses — every single one
It's better than ever
And baby, that's the truth
I wouldn't trade what we have now
For a thousand days of youth
They call us “cute” when we're out to eat
She brushes her foot against my knee
I read the menu upside down
Some young man said, “That fire fades”
My baby laughed and looked my way
I said, “Son, you have yourself a nice day”
It's better than ever
And baby, that's the truth
I wouldn't trade what we have now
For a thousand days of youth
She puts her hand against my chest
Says, “Baby, you know me best”
I say, “And I ain't done learning yet”
We know each other's every move
Still find a way to make it new
I love her more — and Lord, I want her too
It's better than ever
And baby, that's the truth
I wouldn't trade one night with you
For a thousand days of youth
It's better than ever
And I mean every word
It's better than ever
So much better than ever
With you

title: We Don’t Play Rock ’n’ Roll
stanzas: Three brothers I've known since we were boys
Eddie on guitar, Joe's drums made noise
Bill on the keys, and I brought the voice
Ray blows trombone, Cal's on the sax
Mack walks the bass, keeps us on track
We take other gigs, but the blues brings us back
We don't play rock 'n' roll
This band's built on the blues
Give us twelve bars, honey
We'll wear out both your shoes!
Lady in pearls said, “Bésame Mucho”
I tipped my hat and said, “No ma'am, no”
She said, “Then what do you boys know?”
Some fella yelled, “See You Later, Alligator!”
“No sir,” I said, “but you'll thank me later”
Then Eddie played a riff that moved the waiter
We don't play rock 'n' roll
No sir, we play the blues
Hear that guitar!
Hear those horns!
Now watch what your feet can do!
Bill rolls the keys, Joe counts to four
Mack walks the bass, Eddie grins once more
Ray and Cal hit — and they fill the floor!
That lady left her heels beside the door
The man who wanted rock was yelling, “More!”
I said, “That's what you hired us for!”
We don't play rock 'n' roll
No ma'am, we play the blues
Give us twelve bars, honey
We'll wear out both your shoes!
We don't play rock 'n' roll
No, we don't play rock 'n' roll
We play the blues!
Yeah, we play the blues!
“Didn't know the blues could do all that!”
“Well, now you do!”

title: I Never Said Yes
stanzas: Went to a meeting at the neighborhood hall
“Who'll run the block party?” came the call
Everyone looked down — I watched them all
“Solomon, how 'bout you?” she said
I opened my mouth, they clapped instead
Then she handed me a clipboard and fled
I never said yes
I wasn't signing up for this mess
One little glance and they did the rest
No, I never said yes
One wanted tables, one wanted shade
One wanted a banner that hadn't been made
I asked for help — they all walked away
Miss Ruby and Pearl both wanted first prize
I called it a tie — they both rolled their eyes
Now I can't get cake from either side
I never said yes
They asked me to judge who baked the best
Now both of those ladies are unimpressed
No, I never said yes
By sundown, the whole block cheered
The grumpy old neighbor even brought beer
They gave me a plaque, said, “Same time next year!”
Next year, I stayed home, shut the blinds
Told my wife, “They'll pick some other guy”
They voted me in — I wasn't even there!
I never said yes
Wasn't even there to protest
They voted me in while I got some rest
No, I never said yes
I never said yes
No, I never said yes
Not once, not twice
I never said yes!
“Wait a minute... I wasn't even THERE!”

title: Don't Put Me In That Chair
stanzas: My kids came over on a Saturday
Said, “Dad, we brought you something today”
Then two big men came backing up my driveway
Big leather chair with a fancy remote
Heated back and a pillow for my throat
I said, “Who ordered me this padded boat?”
Don't put me in that chair
I got things to do, I got places to be
You can sit there all day, but that ain't me
No, don't put me in that chair!
My daughter said, “Dad, you should take it slow”
I said, “Honey, there's a few things you don't know”
Got a date at eight and a place to go
My son showed me how to raise my feet
Said, “Right here, Dad, you can rest all week”
I said, “Boy, you trying to retire me?”
Don't put me in that chair
I got some gray, but I still got flair
Ain't gonna spend my life just sitting there
No, don't put me in that chair!
Came home late, about half past two
Kicked off my shoes, didn't know what to do
That leather chair was looking pretty good
Sat right down, hit a button by mistake
That thing started humming, made my shoulders shake
I said, “Well, five minutes won't hurt, I guess”
Don't put me in that chair
Well, maybe just a minute, I don't care
But don't you tell my kids you saw me there
No, don't put me in that chair!
Don't put me in that chair
Don't you dare!
Well... maybe right there
“Hey, where's that remote?”

title: I Know That Look
stanzas: Young boy sitting at a table for two
She takes his hand, he forgets what to do
Spills his coffee on his brand-new shoes
She just laughs and wipes his sleeve
He looks at her like he can't believe
I know that look, he's too far gone to leave
I know that look!
Oh, I know that look!
You can fool that boy, but you can't fool me
I know that look!
Yes, I know that look!
I've been where he's going, and it sure ain't free!
Later on, they stop outside a store
She sees a dress that she can't ignore
He checks the price and looks once more
She says, "Don't worry, we can go"
He says, "Let's get it," nice and slow
I know that look, I've said those words before
I know that look!
Oh, I know that look!
You can fool that boy, but you can't fool me
I know that look!
Yes, I know that look!
I've been where he's going, and it sure ain't free!
A lady near me caught my little grin
She moved her chair and asked me to sit in
I knew that look, but I sat down anyway
I know that look!
Oh, I know that look!
You can fool that boy, but you can't fool me
I know that look!
Yes, I know that look!
I've been where he's going, and it sure ain't free!
I know that look!
Oh, I know that look!
Thought I knew it all, now look at me
I know that look!
Yes, I know that look!
Here I go again, and this one's on me!
I know that look!
Oh, I know that look!
She just smiled and I forgot my speech
I know that look!
Yes, I know that look!
Guess that boy ain't so different from me!
I know that look!
Yeah, I know that look!
Oh, here I go again!
I know that look!

title: The Dog Didn’t Like Me
stanzas: Mr. Jones had a dog named Beau
He'd wag at strangers, put on quite a show
But when I came by, he'd tell me where to go
I saved him a biscuit from my plate
Set it by the fence and stood there to wait
He ate that biscuit — then barked at the gate
That dog didn't like me
He'd wag at everybody he could see
But saved his loudest bark for me
That dog didn't like me
One day I sat and played three chords slow
He came right up and watched my fingers go
For once that dog forgot to tell me no
Soon he'd come running when he heard my feet
Lay his big old head across my knee
No guitar needed — just him and me
That dog sure did like me
He'd come running when he'd hear my feet
No song to play, no treat to eat
That dog sure did like me
One day he wasn't waiting by the gate
Mr. Jones said, "Son, he passed away"
They buried him out back that very day
Some days I'd sit by that patch of ground
Play our three chords when no one was around
Funny how quiet a yard can sound
That dog ain't here with me
No warm head resting on my knee
But he was first to love my blues
And I still play for him

title: Back In The Windy City
stanzas: We played a club in Chicago
Some years ago in June
The owner saw our black hats
Said, "Play a country tune!"
I said, "We're from Tennessee,
But buddy, here's the deal..."
Then Eddie hit that shuffle
Then Eddie hit that shuffle
And the whole damn place went wild!
"Not bad for cowboy boots!"
Back in the Windy City
Yeah, we're back again!
Chicago knows these black hats
And we know all our friends!
Back in the Windy City
Back in the Windy City
Too hot or freezing cold
You can keep your crazy weather
But we love this town of yours!
One August night in Chicago
The air conditioning died
The owner yelled, "Stop dancing!"
But nobody even tried
Bill was sweating at the piano
Joe was soaking through his shirt
The owner opened every window
And the band just made it worse!
"He said, 'Can't you play something cooler?'
I said, 'We don't know how!'"
Back in the Windy City
Yeah, we're back again!
Chicago knows these black hats
And we know all our friends!
Back in the Windy City
Too hot or freezing cold
You can keep your crazy weather
But we love this town of yours!
One February in Chicago
Our bus was buried deep
Mack said, "I can't feel my fingers!"
Joe said, "I can't feel my feet!"
"And Eddie said...
'I can't feel a damn thing!'"
A city driver stopped beside us
Said, "You boys enjoying the snow?"
I said, "We love Chicago, mister,
But there's one thing you should know!"
He said, "You boys don't like our winters?"
I said, "Well, here's the truth..."
"We love your town in summer,
And your heating bills ain't cute!"
"But that fella got us outta there.
Good people, Chicago. Good people."
Back in the Windy City
Yeah, we're back again!
Chicago knows these black hats
And we know all our friends!
Back in the Windy City
Too hot or freezing cold
You can keep your crazy weather
But we love this town of yours!
We've played a hundred places
From Memphis to L.A.
But there's something 'bout Chicago
That keeps bringing us this way
They tease us 'bout our accents
We tease 'em 'bout the snow
But when those Chicago folks get dancing
Man, we hate to see 'em go!
Back in the Windy City
Yeah, we're back again!
Chicago knows these black hats
And we know all our friends!
Back in the Windy City
Too hot or freezing cold
You can keep your crazy weather
But we love this town of yours!
"Alright, Chicago!
You know these fellas!
Joe on drums!
Mack 'Lowdown' Turner on bass!
The Rhythm Gang!"
"At the piano, my old buddy Bill!
Give it to 'em, Bill!"
"Cal Brooks on saxophone!
Big Ray Walker on trombone!
Yeah, those Chicago horns!"
"And now, my oldest friend.
Been making trouble together since we were kids!
Eddie!
Take it away, brother!"
"That's my boys!
The Black Hat Guys!
Chicago, we love ya!"
